newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 18.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Energy imports soared, reaching $18.9 billion during the first ten months of this year, up 25.2 percent from a year earlier.

- North Korea has tightened security measures in the northern border area to keep its people from crossing the border. Poverty-stricken North Korean people are reluctant to join the military and the Workers Party, according to a family group of North Korean defectors.

- The June 29 declaration of 1987, a sweeping political statement swearing to accept the results of a popular presidential election and to provide for amnesty of opposition leader Kim Dae-jung was the work of former president Chun Doo Hwan, according to a draft memoir by Chun's wife, which was obtained by Dong-A Ilbo. Chun's successor Roh Tae-woo has consistently claimed that he was the architect of the declaration.

- Korean corporations show signs of reviewing their investments in France in the wake of the French government's cancellation of its decision to sell Thomson Multimedia to Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co, according to Deputy Prime Minister Han Seung-soo. Han expressed dismay over the Thomson affair.

- The strength of U.S. dollar aginst Korean won is expected to continue into next year, topping 860 won per dollar by the end of March, compared with a forecast of 845 won for the end of this year, according to a survey of foreign exchange dealers.
- North Korea doubles guards along China border to head off escapes. Northern residents are also required to have gas masks for possible chemical warfare, defectors told a news conference on Tuesday.
